claims.statement: The application exposes exactly 47 HTTP endpoints, each one a convention-mapped @Action method: 24 on ForeAction, 5 each on CategoryAction, ProductAction and PropertyAction, 3 on ProductImageAction, 2 each on PropertyValueAction and OrderAction, and 1 on UserAction; src/struts.xml contains no <action> element, so endpoint identity exists only in the @Action annotation values (the annotation value is the URL because every method carries an explicit name).

All eight action classes inherit @Namespace("/") and @ParentPackage("basicstruts") from Action4Result, so every URL is root-level with no class-name or package prefix and every endpoint runs the auth-dafault interceptor stack declared in src/struts.xml: authorityInterceptor, categoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor, cartTotalItemNumberInterceptor, then defaultStack.

AuthInterceptor applies only to request URIs starting with /fore: it extracts the substring after the last /fore and compares it against the hard-coded array {home, checkLogin, register, loginAjax, login, product, category, search}. That makes exactly 8 storefront URLs public and the other 16 fore* URLs require a session user (rejected requests get sendRedirect("login.jsp") and the action never runs), while all 23 admin_* URLs receive no auth check of any kind because the prefix test never matches them.

The eight public storefront URLs and the results they return are: forehome -> home.jsp (forward /home.jsp), foreregister -> register.jsp on a duplicate name or the registerSuccessPage redirect to /registerSuccess.jsp on success, forelogin -> login.jsp on bad credentials or the homePage redirect to forehome on success, foreproduct -> product.jsp, forecheckLogin -> success.jsp or fail.jsp, foreloginAjax -> success.jsp or fail.jsp, forecategory -> category.jsp, and foresearch -> searchResult.jsp.

The cart endpoints are forebuyone (binds product.id and num, merges or inserts an OrderItem, returns the buyPage redirect to forebuy?oiids=${oiid} using the singular oiid property), forebuy (binds the repeated oiids array, accumulates total, stores the orderItems list in the session and forwards to buy.jsp), and foreaddCart / forechangeOrderItem / foredeleteOrderItem, which each return success.jsp with body "success".

The checkout and order endpoints form one chain over the session key orderItems: forecreateOrder binds order.address / order.post / order.receiver / order.mobile / order.userMessage, reads the session orderItems written by forebuy, stamps orderCode (yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS), createDate, user and status waitPay, and returns the alipayPage redirect to forealipay?order.id=${order.id}&total=${total} — or the login.jsp forward only when that list is empty, so a request in a session with no orderItems key dereferences null instead of redirecting. forealipay binds order.id and total and returns alipay.jsp, forepayed binds order.id and total and returns payed.jsp, foreconfirmPay binds order.id and returns confirmPay.jsp, foreorderConfirmed binds order.id and returns orderConfirmed.jsp, foredeleteOrder binds order.id and returns success.jsp, and forebought binds nothing and returns bought.jsp.

The review endpoints are forereview (Java method revice(), binds order.id and showonly, returns review.jsp) and foredoreview (binds order.id, product.id and review.content, HTML-escapes the content, saves the review, sets the order status to finish, then sets showonly = true and returns the reviewPage redirect to forereview?order.id=${order.id}&showonly=${showonly}).

Order status is advanced by specific endpoints rather than by one service: forecreateOrder sets waitPay with a generated orderCode and createDate, forepayed sets waitDelivery plus payDate, admin_order_delivery sets waitConfirm plus deliveryDate, foreorderConfirmed sets waitReview plus confirmDate, foredoreview sets finish and inserts the Review row, and foredeleteOrder sets delete (which forebought then filters out).

All 36 result names are declared in the single @Results block on Action4Result: 26 dispatcher forwards (the *.jsp, listXxx and editXxx names, forwarding into web/ or web/admin/) and 10 type="redirect" results, every one of which ends in Page; no concrete action class declares @Result, @Results, @Namespace or @ParentPackage, and the current source is consistent — every declared name is returned by at least one @Action method.

Six of the ten redirect results interpolate their location with OGNL against the acting action instance — buyPage to forebuy?oiids=${oiid}, alipayPage to forealipay?order.id=${order.id}&total=${total}, reviewPage to forereview?order.id=${order.id}&showonly=${showonly}, listPropertyPage to /admin_property_list?category.id=${property.category.id}, listProductPage to /admin_product_list?category.id=${product.category.id}, listProductImagePage to /admin_productImage_list?product.id=${productImage.product.id} — while the other four (listCategoryPage, listOrderPage, homePage, registerSuccessPage) have fixed targets. Each interpolated parameter name must match a property on the receiving action, and because the expressions navigate associations the entity must be persistent (post-t2p()) before the result is returned.

Endpoint inputs are bound only through public setters on the Action4* chain, in the dotted OGNL shapes the callers actually send: entity properties such as category.id, category.name, product.id, order.address, orderItem.id, productImage.type, propertyValue.value and user.name/user.password; scalars num, oiid, oiids (repeated), total, keyword, sort, showonly; page.start via the Page object; and the multipart file field img. Adding a bindable name means adding a field plus public setter to Action4Pojo, Action4Pagination, Action4Parameter or Action4Upload, since no application-level parameter whitelist exists.

Exactly three URLs bind a multipart upload under the field name img — admin_category_add, admin_category_update and admin_productImage_add — and each writes the file into the web application directory keyed by the persisted entity id (img/category/<id>.jpg, or img/productSingle/ and img/productDetail/ with the 56x56 and 217x190 derivatives for a type_single product image).

Five admin list URLs bind page.start — admin_category_list, admin_property_list, admin_product_list, admin_order_list and admin_user_list — and the pagination widget emits only page.start plus the action's page.param value, which PropertyAction.list and ProductAction.list set to "&category.id=<id>" (read from the id-only bound parent before t2p() replaces it) so the parent filter survives the round trip. page.count is never sent by any caller; it comes from Page's no-arg constructor default of 5.

Seven endpoints answer with the plain-text payload results success.jsp (body "success") or fail.jsp (body "fail") for AJAX callers: forecheckLogin and foreloginAjax return one of the two, foreaddCart, forechangeOrderItem, foredeleteOrderItem, foredeleteOrder and admin_propertyValue_update return success.jsp, and the calling page scripts compare the response against the literal "success" (falling back to location.href = "login.jsp" on mismatch).

The storefront order page calls an unguarded back-office endpoint: the "催卖家发货" button in web/include/cart/boughtPage.jsp issues an AJAX GET to admin_order_delivery?order.id=${o.id}, which is the same OrderAction.delivery endpoint the admin list uses and is reached without any auth check because its URI does not start with /fore.

ProductAction.list computes the paging total for the product list with propertyService.total(category), so the number of pages rendered for admin_product_list is derived from the category's property count rather than its product count; the sibling list actions use their own service.

foresearch binds only keyword and hard-codes a 20-row window (productService.search(keyword, 0, 20)) with no page.start, so the storefront search is the only list endpoint that cannot be paged; forecategory's sort parameter accepts the five values wired in include/category/sortBar.jsp (all, review, date, saleCount, price) and exists only in that JSP's links and ForeAction.category's switch.

The storefront wrapper JSPs that results forward to are also directly reachable, because a .jsp URL is not an action candidate and passes through the Struts filter to the JSP servlet: such a hit runs no interceptor and renders with empty action data, and the admin JSPs' relative links without a leading slash (href="admin_category_list", href="admin_productImage_delete?productImage.id=...") resolve to root-namespace URLs only when the browser's URL is the action URL rather than /admin/<file>.jsp.

The fraction of the request displayed on the category and home pages is capped by the request parameter categorycount (default 100 when absent), but no JSP or JavaScript in the repository emits that parameter, so the cap can only be changed by typing it into the URL; the same is true of the display-only total and showonly parameters, which are read by the JSPs through param.* rather than by the action bodies.

login.jsp is simultaneously a result name (a forward target used by forelogin and forecreateOrder) and a directly served JSP path, so both the internal forward and a plain GET /login.jsp render the same page — the same coincidence of result name and file name holds for the other *.jsp results.

The registration form's submit control is wrapped in an anchor to registerSuccess.jsp while the enclosing form posts to foreregister, and its repeat-password input carries no name attribute and is therefore never submitted; which of the POST and the anchor navigation wins in a browser is not determined anywhere in the repository 【人工评审待确认】.

The two admin product write endpoints gained one request parameter each: admin_product_add and admin_product_update both bind product.remark, emitted by the 备注 input of the add form in web/admin/listProduct.jsp and the edit form in web/admin/editProduct.jsp (the only two JSPs in the repository that emit that name). The name is an ordinary dotted property, so the params interceptor sets it on Action4Pojo.product exactly like product.name, and no action code names the field — ProductAction contains no reference to remark, so add() and update() persist it through the same generic productService.save/update call as every other scalar, with no new URL or result name.

remark is a plainly mapped String on the Product entity (declared without any annotation, unlike the @Transient render fields), so the value is written into the product row; the column exists only because the H2 seed script appends ALTER TABLE product ADD COLUMN remark varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL after the 85 positional INSERT statements, while its own CREATE TABLE product omits the column — which is why the seeded products show as blank in the 备注 column.

The remark value round-trips inside the back office only: admin_product_list renders it as the 备注 column via ${p.remark} and admin_product_edit echoes the stored value into the edit input via value="${product.remark}", while no storefront JSP reads remark and the field participates in no price, stock, image, property, order, paging or sorting logic.

ProductAction.update reloads the existing row from the database only to copy its createDate onto the bound object, because no admin product form posts createDate; remark is never reloaded, so it is written purely from the request — the edit form echoes the stored value so an unchanged submit round-trips it, but an emptied field is stored as emptied.
